name: Rory O'More Bridge
facts: Rory O'More Bridge, originally a 1670 wooden structure called Barrack Bridge, earned the nickname Bloody Bridge after ferrymen’s failed attempts to destroy it, resulting in four deaths during a rescue.
The current cast‑iron span, completed in 1859, was fabricated in St Helens, Lancashire, and shipped in pieces, then assembled on granite abutments beside the River Liffey.
Renamed in the 1930s for rebel leader Rory O'More, the bridge replaced a 1704 stone bridge and survived the arrival of the railway, which prompted the relocation of the nearby Richmond Tower.
